newsitem.title: USA: Heat sends Washington workers home.
newsitem.headline: Heat sends Washington workers home.

text.p: Oppressive heat and unhealthful air brought trash collection and road repairs to a halt in the nation's capital on Tuesday when the District of Columbia sent almost 500 employees home early.
As temperatures flirted with the century mark for the third day in a row and ozone pollution reached critical levels, the D.C. government also opened "cooling centers" in downtown Washington.

Residents without air conditioning or simply suffering in the heat can use the centers -- set up in government buildings -- to take a break and cool down. Some also make shower facilities available to the public.

Forecasters predicted that Tuesday's temperature could exceed the record of 100 degrees after highs of 97 Sunday and Monday. With the humidity factored in, the heat index was expected to top 105 degrees.

The D.C. Department of Public Works decided to send 476 employees home at noon because of the dangerous conditions. Affected services included residential trash collection, street sweeping and road repairs.
The combination of pollutants and hot stagnant air prompted government agencies to put in place their Ozone Action Day program.
Commuters were urged to use public transport, motorists to avoid refueling their cars during daylight hours and gardeners to hold off mowing their lawns until evening.
Some city bus systems in suburban Maryland offered free rides throughout the day, hoping to cut the number of cars traveling the area's habitually congested streets.

As the ozone standards set by the Environmental Protection Agency were surpassed, officials declared a "Code Red" and advised the elderly, the very young and those with health problems to stay indoors.
When temperatures are high, skies clear and winds too light to move the air effectively, particles and gases, including ozone -- mostly from exhaust emissions -- build up to unhealthy levels.
Washington experienced just one Code Red day last summer, but has had three in a row this week. Forecasters said they expected the heat wave to continue for at least several more days.
